statement: U010 is answered: regime-conditioned temporal weighting is unnecessary once the temporal term is conditioned on validity intervals. The opposite-direction tension between current and historical queries is a property of monotone elapsed-time decay (which always rewards recency) rather than of the task itself; a single interval-membership term targets the version in force at the query date for any query date, and the evidence shows one regime-independent as-of-date rule retrieves correctly for both current and historical questions. Query-regime conditioning is therefore subsumed by interval-aware scoring and should not be pursued as a separate mechanism.
